\title{Extremal finite graphs}
\author{}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\paragraph{Vertex cloning.} In \(\operatorname{clone}(G,s,t)\), vertex \(t\) takes the neighbors of \(s\) in \(G\), excluding \(t\) itself. All edges away from \(t\) are preserved.

\section*{Definitions}
\paragraph{Is turan maximal.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:1}\paperlineanchor{defeq:1}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:1}{D1})} Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(G,\allowbreak{} r) = (G\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land (\forall H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \forall \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|))\).

\paragraph{Turan graph.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:2}\paperlineanchor{defeq:2}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:2}{D2})} Let \(n\) and \(r\) be natural numbers. Then \(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r) = (\text{the graph on }\operatorname{Fin}(n)\text{ in which }v\text{ and }w\text{ are adjacent exactly when }\operatorname{val}(v) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(w) \bmod r)\).

\paragraph{Setoid.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:3}\paperlineanchor{defeq:3}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:3}{D3})} Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,relation}(G,\allowbreak{} r) = (\text{the equivalence relation }(\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))\text{ on }V)\).

\paragraph{Inst decidable rel r.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:4}\paperlineanchor{defeq:4}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:4}{D4})} Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{inst\,Decidable\,Rel\,R} = \operatorname{infer\,Instance\,As}(\operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2})))\).

\paragraph{Finpartition.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:5}\paperlineanchor{defeq:5}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:5}{D5})} Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume equality on \(V\) is decidable. Then \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r) = (\text{the partition into equivalence classes of }\operatorname{nonadjacency\,relation}(G,\allowbreak{} r))\).

\paragraph{Inst decidable rel adj.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:6}\paperlineanchor{defeq:6}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:6}{D6})} Let \(n\) and \(r\) be natural numbers. Then \(\operatorname{inst\,Decidable\,Rel\,Adj} = \operatorname{id}\left(\operatorname{infer\,Instance}\right)\).

\subsection*{Prerequisites}
\begin{description}
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:416e642e6c656674}\paperlink{premise:416e642e6c656674}{P1.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:416e642e6c656674}\textbf{Left.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Assume \(a \land b\). Then \(a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:416e642e7269676874}\paperlink{premise:416e642e7269676874}{P2.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:416e642e7269676874}\textbf{Right.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Assume \(a \land b\). Then \(b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:436c6173736963616c2e656d}\paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e656d}{P3.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:436c6173736963616c2e656d}\textbf{Em.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(p \lor \neg p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}\paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}{P4.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}\textbf{Not forall.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Then \(\neg (\forall x\, :\, \alpha,\; p(x)) \iff (\exists x\, :\, \alpha,\; \neg p(x))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e2e69734c74}\paperlink{premise:46696e2e69734c74}{P5.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e2e69734c74}\textbf{Is less than.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Let \(\mathit{self}\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\). Then \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{self}) < n\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e2e6d6b2e696e6a4571}\paperlink{premise:46696e2e6d6b2e696e6a4571}{P6.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e2e6d6b2e696e6a4571}\textbf{Injectivity equals.} Let \(n\) and \(\mathit{val}\) be natural numbers. Let \(\mathit{isLt}\) be a proof of \(\mathit{val} < n\). Let \(\mathit{val}_{1}\) be a natural number. Let \(\mathit{isLt}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\mathit{val}_{1} < n\). Then \((\operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{val}) = \operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{val}_{1})) = (\mathit{val} = \mathit{val}_{1})\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}\paperlink{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}{P7.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}\textbf{Val injectivity.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Let \(a\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\). Let \(b\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\). Then \(\operatorname{val}(a) = \operatorname{val}(b) \iff a = b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e497345717569706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7061727450726573657276696e674571756976}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e497345717569706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7061727450726573657276696e674571756976}{P8.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e497345717569706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7061727450726573657276696e674571756976}\textbf{Exists part preserving equiv.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Equipartition}\left(P\right)\). Then \(\exists f\, :\, \operatorname{Bij}(s,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Fin}(|s|)),\; \forall a\, :\, s,\; \forall b\, :\, s,\; \operatorname{part}(P,\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(P,\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{val}(f(a)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(P)| = \operatorname{val}(f(b)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(P)|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e636172645f70617274735f6c655f63617264}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e636172645f70617274735f6c655f63617264}{P9.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e636172645f70617274735f6c655f63617264}\textbf{Cardinality parts at most cardinality.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Then \(\left|\operatorname{parts}\left(P\right)\right| \le \left|s\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7375627365745f706172745f62696a4f6e}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7375627365745f706172745f62696a4f6e}{P10.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7375627365745f706172745f62696a4f6e}\textbf{Exists subset part bij on.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Then \(\exists r\, :\, \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\alpha),\; r \subseteq s \land \operatorname{Bij\,On}(\operatorname{part}(P),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(r),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(\operatorname{parts}(P)))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6966665f706172745f65715f70617274}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6966665f706172745f65715f70617274}{P11.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6966665f706172745f65715f70617274}\textbf{Membership part if and only if part equals part.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a \in s\). Assume \(b \in s\). Then \(a \in \operatorname{part}(P,\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{part}(P,\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(P,\allowbreak{} b)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6f665365746f69645f6966665f72656c}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6f665365746f69645f6966665f72656c}{P12.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6f665365746f69645f6966665f72656c}\textbf{Membership part of setoid if and only if rel.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Fix a finite enumeration of \(\alpha\). Let \(s\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Setoid}\left(\alpha\right)\). Assume the relation \(s\) is decidable. Let \(b\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(b \in \operatorname{part}\left(\text{the partition into equivalence classes of }s, a\right) \iff a \sim_{s} b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6e6f6e656d7074795f6f665f6d656d5f7061727473}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6e6f6e656d7074795f6f665f6d656d5f7061727473}{P13.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6e6f6e656d7074795f6f665f6d656d5f7061727473}\textbf{Nonempty of membership parts.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Let \(a\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a \in \operatorname{parts}\left(P\right)\). Then \(a\ne\varnothing\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6e6f745f697345717569706172746974696f6e}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6e6f745f697345717569706172746974696f6e}{P14.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6e6f745f697345717569706172746974696f6e}\textbf{Not is equipartition.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Then \(\neg \operatorname{Is\,Equipartition}(P) \iff (\exists a\, :\, \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\alpha),\; a \in \operatorname{parts}(P) \land (\exists b\, :\, \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\alpha),\; b \in \operatorname{parts}(P) \land |b| + 1 < |a|))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e706172745f65715f6f665f6d656d}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e706172745f65715f6f665f6d656d}{P15.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e706172745f65715f6f665f6d656d}\textbf{Part equals of membership.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be finite subsets of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Assume \(t \in \operatorname{parts}\left(P\right)\). Assume \(a \in t\). Then \(\operatorname{part}\left(P, a\right) = t\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e706172745f6d656d}\paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e706172745f6d656d}{P16.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e706172745f6d656d}\textbf{Part membership.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(P\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Finpartition}\left(s\right)\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{part}\left(P, a\right) \in \operatorname{parts}\left(P\right) \iff a \in s\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f65715f6f665f6571756976}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f65715f6f665f6571756976}{P17.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f65715f6f665f6571756976}\textbf{Cardinality equals of equiv.} Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be types. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(t\) be a finite subset of \(\beta\). Let \(i\) be a bijection from \(s\) to \(t\). Then \(\left|s\right| = \left|t\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f6c655f63617264}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f6c655f63617264}{P18.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f6c655f63617264}\textbf{Cardinality at most cardinality.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be finite subsets of \(\alpha\). Assume \(s \subseteq t\). Then \(\left|s\right| \le \left|t\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f7364696666}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f7364696666}{P19.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f7364696666}\textbf{Cardinality sdiff.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be finite subsets of \(\alpha\). Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Assume \(s \subseteq t\). Then \(\left|t \setminus s\right| = \left|t\right| - \left|s\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f73696e676c65746f6e}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f73696e676c65746f6e}{P20.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f73696e676c65746f6e}\textbf{Cardinality singleton.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(\left|\{a\}\right| = 1\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e65715f6f665f7375627365745f6f665f636172645f6c65}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e65715f6f665f7375627365745f6f665f636172645f6c65}{P21.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e65715f6f665f7375627365745f6f665f636172645f6c65}\textbf{Equals of subset of cardinality at most.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be finite subsets of \(\alpha\). Assume \(s \subseteq t\). Assume \(\left|t\right| \le \left|s\right|\). Then \(s = t\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f6d61785f696d616765}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f6d61785f696d616765}{P22.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f6d61785f696d616765}\textbf{Exists max image.} Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be types. Equip \(\alpha\) with a linear order. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\beta\). Let \(f\) be a function of type \(\beta \to \alpha\). Assume \(s\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\exists x\, :\, \beta,\; x \in s \land (\forall x^{'}\, :\, \beta,\; x^{'} \in s \implies f(x^{'}) \le f(x))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f6e655f6d61705f65715f6f665f636172645f6c745f6f665f6d6170735f746f}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f6e655f6d61705f65715f6f665f636172645f6c745f6f665f6d6170735f746f}{P23.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f6e655f6d61705f65715f6f665f636172645f6c745f6f665f6d6170735f746f}\textbf{Exists differs from map equals of cardinality less than of maps to.} Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be types. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(t\) be a finite subset of \(\beta\). Assume \(\left|t\right| < \left|s\right|\). Let \(f\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \beta\). Assume \(\forall a\, :\, \alpha,\; a \in s \implies f\left(a\right) \in t\). Then \(\exists x\, :\, \alpha,\; x \in s \land (\exists y\, :\, \alpha,\; y \in s \land (x \ne y \land f(x) = f(y)))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f7375627365745f636172645f6571}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f7375627365745f636172645f6571}{P24.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f7375627365745f636172645f6571}\textbf{Exists subset cardinality equals.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(n\) be a natural number. Assume \(n \le \left|s\right|\). Then \(\exists t\, :\, \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\alpha),\; t \subseteq s \land \left|t\right| = n\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e657874}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e657874}{P25.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e657874}\textbf{Ext.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s_{1}\) and \(s_{2}\) be finite subsets of \(\alpha\). Assume \(\forall a\, :\, \alpha,\; a \in s_{1} \iff a \in s_{2}\). Then \(s_{1} = s_{2}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e66696c7465725f636172645f6164645f66696c7465725f6e65675f636172645f65715f63617264}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e66696c7465725f636172645f6164645f66696c7465725f6e65675f636172645f65715f63617264}{P26.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e66696c7465725f636172645f6164645f66696c7465725f6e65675f636172645f65715f63617264}\textbf{Filter cardinality sum filter neg cardinality equals cardinality.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Assume the predicate \(p\) is decidable. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) of type \(\Pi_{x\, :\, \alpha}\, \operatorname{Decidable}\left(\neg p\left(x\right)\right)\). Then \(\left|\{x\in s \mid p(x)\}\right| + \left|\{a\in s \mid \neg p\left(a\right)\}\right| = \left|s\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e7365742e66696c7465725f65715f656d7074795f696666}\paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e66696c7465725f65715f656d7074795f696666}{P27.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e7365742e66696c7465725f65715f656d7074795f696666}\textbf{Filter equals empty if and only if.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Assume the predicate \(p\) is decidable. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Then \(\{x\in s \mid p(x)\} = \varnothing \iff (\forall x\, :\, \alpha,\; x \in s \implies \neg p(x))\).

\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f7375625f737562}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f7375625f737562}{P68.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f7375625f737562}\textbf{Of nat difference difference.} Let \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) be natural numbers. Then \(a - b - c = a - \left(b + c\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}{P69.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}\textbf{Difference congruence.} Let \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\) be integers. Assume \(a = b\). Assume \(c = d\). Then \(a - c = b - d\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}{P70.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}\textbf{Sum eval.} Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Linear\,Combo}\). Let \(v\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(l_{1} + l_{2},\allowbreak{} v) = \operatorname{eval}(l_{1},\allowbreak{} v) + \operatorname{eval}(l_{2},\allowbreak{} v)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}{P71.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}\textbf{Coordinate eval 0.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\) be an integer. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t)) = \mathit{a0}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}{P72.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}\textbf{Coordinate eval 1.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\) and \(\mathit{a1}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t))) = \mathit{a1}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f32}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f32}{P73.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f32}\textbf{Coordinate eval 2.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), and \(\mathit{a2}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(2),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t)))) = \mathit{a2}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f33}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f33}{P74.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f33}\textbf{Coordinate eval 3.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), \(\mathit{a2}\), and \(\mathit{a3}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(3),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a3}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t))))) = \mathit{a3}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f34}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f34}{P75.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f34}\textbf{Coordinate eval 4.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), \(\mathit{a2}\), \(\mathit{a3}\), and \(\mathit{a4}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(4),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a3}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a4}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t)))))) = \mathit{a4}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f35}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f35}{P76.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f35}\textbf{Coordinate eval 5.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), \(\mathit{a2}\), \(\mathit{a3}\), \(\mathit{a4}\), and \(\mathit{a5}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(5),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a3}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a4}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a5}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t))))))) = \mathit{a5}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f36}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f36}{P77.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f36}\textbf{Coordinate eval 6.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), \(\mathit{a2}\), \(\mathit{a3}\), \(\mathit{a4}\), \(\mathit{a5}\), and \(\mathit{a6}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(6),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a3}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a4}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a5}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a6}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t)))))))) = \mathit{a6}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f37}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f37}{P78.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f37}\textbf{Coordinate eval 7.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), \(\mathit{a2}\), \(\mathit{a3}\), \(\mathit{a4}\), \(\mathit{a5}\), \(\mathit{a6}\), and \(\mathit{a7}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(7),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a3}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a4}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a5}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a6}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a7}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t))))))))) = \mathit{a7}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}{P79.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}\textbf{Difference eval.} Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Linear\,Combo}\). Let \(v\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(l_{1} - l_{2},\allowbreak{} v) = \operatorname{eval}(l_{1},\allowbreak{} v) - \operatorname{eval}(l_{2},\allowbreak{} v)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}{P80.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}\textbf{Combo sat'.} Let \(s\) and \(t\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Constraint}\). Let \(a\) be an integer. Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Let \(b\) be an integer. Let \(y\) and \(v\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(s, x, v\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(t, y, v\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}combo}(a,\allowbreak{} s,\allowbreak{} b,\allowbreak{} t),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Coeffs\mathord{:}combo}(a,\allowbreak{} x,\allowbreak{} b,\allowbreak{} y),\allowbreak{} v) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}{P81.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}\textbf{Tidy sat.} Let \(s\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Constraint}\). Let \(x\) and \(v\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(s, x, v\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{tidy\,Constraint}(s,\allowbreak{} x),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{tidy\,Coeffs}(s,\allowbreak{} x),\allowbreak{} v) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}{P82.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}\textbf{Mtr.} Let \(p\) and \(q\) be propositions. Assume \(\neg q \implies \neg p\). Assume \(p\). Then \(q\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f616e645f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f616e645f6571}{P83.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f616e645f6571}\textbf{Not and equals.} Let \(p\) and \(q\) be propositions. Then \(\left(\neg \left(p \land q\right)\right) = \left(p \implies \neg q\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}{P84.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}\textbf{Not forall equals.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(s\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Then \((\neg (\forall x\, :\, \alpha,\; s(x))) = (\exists x\, :\, \alpha,\; \neg s(x))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696666}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696666}{P85.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696666}\textbf{Not if and only if.} Let \(p\) and \(q\) be propositions. Then \(\left(\neg \left(p \iff q\right)\right) = \left(p \land \neg q \lor \neg p \land q\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}{P86.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}\textbf{Not implies equals.} Let \(p\) and \(q\) be propositions. Then \(\left(\neg \left(p \implies q\right)\right) = \left(p \land \neg q\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}{P87.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}\textbf{Not at most equals.} Let \(\beta\) be a type. Equip \(\beta\) with a linear order. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\beta\). Then \(\left(\neg \left(a \le b\right)\right) = \left(b < a\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}{P88.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}\textbf{Not differs from equals.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\left(\neg \left(x \ne y\right)\right) = \left(x = y\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e6f745f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e6f745f6571}{P89.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e6f745f6571}\textbf{Not not equals.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(\left(\neg \left(\neg p\right)\right) = p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6f725f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6f725f6571}{P90.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6f725f6571}\textbf{Not or equals.} Let \(p\) and \(q\) be propositions. Then \(\left(\neg \left(p \lor q\right)\right) = \left(\neg p \land \neg q\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6164645f7375625f63616e63656c}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f7375625f63616e63656c}{P91.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6164645f7375625f63616e63656c}\textbf{Sum difference cancel.} Let \(n\) and \(m\) be natural numbers. Then \(n + m - m = n\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}{P92.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}\textbf{Inst canonically ordered sum.} \(\operatorname{Canonically\,Ordered\,Add}\left(\mathbb{N}\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}{P93.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}\textbf{Inst is ordered sum monoid.} \(\text{translation preserves order on }\mathbb{N}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}{P94.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}\textbf{Inst is ordered cancel sum monoid.} \(\text{translation preserves and reflects order on }\mathbb{N}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}{P95.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}\textbf{Inst ordered difference.} \(\operatorname{Ordered\,Sub}\left(\mathbb{N}\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c655f6f665f6e6f745f6c74}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c655f6f665f6e6f745f6c74}{P96.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c655f6f665f6e6f745f6c74}\textbf{At most of not less than.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(\neg \left(a < b\right)\). Then \(b \le a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c742e62617365}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c742e62617365}{P97.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c742e62617365}\textbf{Base.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(n < n + 1\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}{P98.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}\textbf{Less than of not at most.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(\neg \left(a \le b\right)\). Then \(b < a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f6e655f696666}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f6e655f696666}{P99.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f6e655f696666}\textbf{Less than one if and only if.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(n < 1 \iff n = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}{P100.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}\textbf{Mod equals of less than.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(a < b\). Then \(a \bmod b = a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f6c74}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f6c74}{P101.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f6c74}\textbf{Mod less than.} Let \(x\) and \(y\) be natural numbers. Assume \(y > 0\). Then \(x \bmod y < y\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f73656c66}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f73656c66}{P102.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f73656c66}\textbf{Mod self.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(n \bmod n = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}{P103.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}\textbf{Mod zero.} Let \(a\) be a natural number. Then \(a \bmod 0 = a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}{P104.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}\textbf{Positivity of differs from zero.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Assume \(n \ne 0\). Then \(0 < n\).

\section{Defs}
\begin{lemma}[{At most if and only if equals}]\label{theorem:1}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(H\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume \(H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\). Then \(G \subseteq H \iff G = H\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(G \subseteq H\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e6564676546696e7365745f696e6a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e6564676546696e7365745f696e6a}}, we obtain \(E(G) = E(H) \iff G = H\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e6564676546696e7365745f7375627365745f6564676546696e736574}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e6564676546696e7365745f7375627365745f6564676546696e736574}}, we obtain \(E(G) \subseteq E(H) \iff G \subseteq H\).
Use the hypothesis \(G \subseteq H\).
By the reverse implication, we obtain \(E(G) \subseteq E(H)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
Taking the second conjunct, we obtain \(\left|E(H)\right| \le \left|E(G)\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e65715f6f665f7375627365745f6f665f636172645f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e7365742e65715f6f665f7375627365745f6f665f636172645f6c65}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Sym2}\left(V\right)\), we obtain \(E(G) = E(H)\).
By the forward implication, we obtain \(G = H\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:6c655f6f665f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6c655f6f665f6571}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V)\), we obtain \(G = H \implies G \subseteq H\).
Together the two implications give the equivalence. Hence \(G \subseteq H \iff G = H\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[{Turan graph zero}]\label{theorem:2}
Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} 0) = \operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n)).\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(a\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(b\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}} and \paperlink{premise:6966665f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6966665f73656c66}} gives \(\operatorname{val}(a) = \operatorname{val}(b) \iff a = b\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f6966665f6e6f74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f6966665f6e6f74}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(a) \ne \operatorname{val}(b) \iff a \ne b\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(a) \bmod 0 \ne \operatorname{val}(b) \bmod 0 \iff a \ne b\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e746f705f61646a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e746f705f61646a}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(a) \bmod 0 \ne \operatorname{val}(b) \bmod 0 \iff a \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} b\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(a \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} 0)} b \iff a \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} b\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((a \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} 0)} b) = (a \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} b)\).
\end{proofstep}
By function extensionality, we obtain \((v \mapsto a \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} 0)} v) = (v \mapsto a \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} v)\).
\end{proofstep}
By function extensionality, we obtain \(\operatorname{Adj}(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} 0)) = \operatorname{Adj}(\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n)))\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e657874}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e657874}} with \(V = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\), we obtain \(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(n, 0\right) = \operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[{Turan graph equals top}]\label{theorem:3}
Let \(n\) and \(r\) be natural numbers. Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r) = \operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n)) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r.\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
By \paperlink{premise:66756e6578745f696666}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:66756e6578745f696666}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\), we obtain \((v \mapsto x \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)} v) = (v \mapsto x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} v) \iff (\forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (x \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)} x_{1}) = (x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(((v \mapsto x \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)} v) = (v \mapsto x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} v)) = (\forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (x \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)} x_{1}) = (x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1}))\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e746f705f61646a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e746f705f61646a}} with \(V = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\) and \(v = x\) and \(w = x_{1}\), we obtain \(x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1} \iff x \ne x_{1}\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(\left(x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1}\right) = \left(x \ne x_{1}\right)\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \(((\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) = (x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1})) = ((\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) = (x \ne x_{1}))\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\), we obtain \((\forall a\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(a) \bmod r) = (x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} a)) = (\forall a\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(a) \bmod r) = (x \ne a))\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
By \paperlink{premise:65715f6966665f696666}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f6966665f696666}}, we obtain \((\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) = (x \ne x_{1}) \iff (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x \ne x_{1})\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(((\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) = (x \ne x_{1})) = (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x \ne x_{1})\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\), we obtain \((\forall a\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(a) \bmod r) = (x \ne a)) = (\forall a\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(a) \bmod r \iff x \ne a)\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
By \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f6966665f6e6f74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f6966665f6e6f74}}, we obtain \((\neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) \iff \neg (x = x_{1})) \iff (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) \iff \neg (x = x_{1})) = (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\), we obtain \((\forall a\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(a) \bmod r) \iff \neg (x = a)) = (\forall a\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(a) \bmod r \iff x = a)\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\) and \(s = x_{1} \mapsto \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}\), we obtain \((\neg (\forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})) = (\exists x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696666}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696666}} with \(p = \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r\) and \(q = x = x_{1}\), we obtain \((\neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})) = (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \land \neg (x = x_{1}) \lor \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) \land x = x_{1})\).
\end{proofstep}
By function extensionality, we obtain \((x_{1} \mapsto \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})) = (x_{1} \mapsto \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \land \neg (x = x_{1}) \lor \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) \land x = x_{1})\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \((\exists x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})) = (\exists x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \land \neg (x = x_{1}) \lor \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) \land x = x_{1})\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\neg (\forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})) = (\exists x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \land \neg (x = x_{1}) \lor \neg (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) \land x = x_{1})\).
\end{proofstep}
Assume \(r \ne 0 \land r < n\).
Construct an element of \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\) with val \(0\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Is less than.}\enspace
Use the hypothesis \(r \ne 0 \land r < n\).
Taking the first conjunct, we obtain \(r \ne 0\).
By \paperlink{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}}, we obtain \(0 < r\).
Use the hypothesis \(r \ne 0 \land r < n\).
Taking the second conjunct, we obtain \(r < n\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\), we obtain \(0 < n\).
Construct an element of \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\) with val \(r\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Is less than.}\enspace
Use the hypothesis \(r \ne 0 \land r < n\).
Taking the second conjunct, we obtain \(r < n\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e7a65726f5f6d6f64}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e7a65726f5f6d6f64}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f73656c66}}, \paperlink{premise:46696e2e6d6b2e696e6a4571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e2e6d6b2e696e6a4571}}, \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e706f735f6f665f6e655f7a65726f}}, \paperlink{premise:416e642e6c656674}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:416e642e6c656674}} (using \(r \ne 0 \land r < n\)), \paperlink{premise:416e642e7269676874}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:416e642e7269676874}} (using \(r \ne 0 \land r < n\)), \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{premise:4e652e73796d6d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e652e73796d6d}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, \paperlink{premise:616e645f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:616e645f73656c66}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f747275655f65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f747275655f65715f66616c7365}} and \paperlink{premise:6f725f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f725f66616c7365}} gives \(0 \bmod r = r \bmod r \land \neg (\operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(0) = \operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(r)) \lor 0 \bmod r \ne r \bmod r \land \operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(0) = \operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(r)\).
This witness proves existence. Hence \(\exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; 0 \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \land \operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(0) \ne x \lor 0 \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \land \operatorname{Fin\mathord{:}mk}(0) = x\).
This witness proves existence. Hence \(\exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \exists x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \land x \ne x_{1} \lor \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \land x = x_{1}\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}}, \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6f725f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6f725f6571}}, \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}}, \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}}, \paperlink{premise:66756e657874}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:66756e657874}} and the identity established above in the preceding result gives \(\neg (r = 0 \lor n \le r) \implies \neg (\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1})\).
Use the hypothesis \(\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}}, we obtain \(r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Use the hypothesis \(r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(r = 0\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(a_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
Fix \(b\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f7a65726f}}, \paperlink{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}} and \paperlink{premise:6966665f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6966665f73656c66}} gives \(\operatorname{val}(a_{1}) \bmod 0 = \operatorname{val}(b) \bmod 0 \iff a_{1} = b\).
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \(r = 0\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(0 = r\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(n \le r\).
Fix \(a_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
Fix \(b\) in \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e2e76616c5f696e6a}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}}, \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e735f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e735f6c65}} (using \(n \le r\)) and \paperlink{premise:46696e2e69734c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e2e69734c74}} gives \(\operatorname{val}(a_{1}) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(b) \bmod r \iff a_{1} = b\).
\end{proofstep}
The two alternatives exhaust the cases. Hence \(\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}\).
\end{proofstep}
Together the two implications give the equivalence. Hence \((\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x = x_{1}) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} and the identity established above in the preceding result gives \((\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r \iff x \ne x_{1}) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} and the identity established above in the preceding result gives \((\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) = (x \ne x_{1})) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} and the identity established above in the preceding result gives \((\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (\operatorname{val}(x) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(x_{1}) \bmod r) = (x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1})) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \((\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; \forall x_{1}\, :\, \operatorname{Fin}(n),\; (x \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)} x_{1}) = (x \sim_{\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))} x_{1})) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:66756e6578745f696666}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:66756e6578745f696666}}, \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}} and the identity established above in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{Adj}(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)) = \operatorname{Adj}(\operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n))) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e6578745f696666}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e6578745f696666}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r) = \operatorname{complete\,graph}(\operatorname{Fin}(n)) \iff r = 0 \lor n \le r\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[{Turan graph clique free}]\label{theorem:4}
Let \(n\) and \(r\) be natural numbers. Assume \(0 < r\). Then \(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(n, r\right)\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}

\begin{theorem}[{Not clique free}]\label{theorem:5}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Assume \(r \le \left|V\right|\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Then \(G\text{ contains a clique of size }r\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Assume \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }r\).
Use the hypothesis \(r \le \left|V\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f7375627365745f636172645f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e7365742e6578697374735f7375627365745f636172645f6571}} with \(s = V\), we obtain \(\exists t\, :\, \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V),\; t \subseteq V \land \left|t\right| = r\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(K\) in \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V)\).
Assume \(K \subseteq V \land \left|K\right| = r\).
Use the hypothesis \(K \subseteq V \land \left|K\right| = r\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(K \subseteq V\).
Assume \(\left|K\right| = r\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\left|K\right| \le \left|V\right|\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, \left|K\right|\right)\).
Assume \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }\left|K\right|\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6d656d5f636f65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e7365742e6d656d5f636f65}}, we obtain \(x \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \iff x \in K\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(\left(x \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K)\right) = \left(x \in K\right)\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(y\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6d656d5f636f65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e7365742e6d656d5f636f65}}, we obtain \(y \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \iff y \in K\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(\left(y \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K)\right) = \left(y \in K\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \((\neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y) = (\neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y)\).
By \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}} with \(p_{1} = y \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K)\) and \(p_{2} = y \in K\) and \(q_{1} = \neg \left(x = y\right) \implies x \sim_{G} y\) and \(q_{2} = \neg \left(x = y\right) \implies x \sim_{G} y\), we obtain \((y \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \implies \neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y) = (y \in K \implies \neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y)\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \((\forall a\, :\, V,\; a \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \implies \neg (x = a) \implies x \sim_{G} a) = (\forall a\, :\, V,\; a \in K \implies \neg (x = a) \implies x \sim_{G} a)\).
By \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}} with \(p_{1} = x \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K)\) and \(p_{2} = x \in K\) and \(q_{1} = \forall a\, :\, V,\; a \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \implies \neg (x = a) \implies x \sim_{G} a\) and \(q_{2} = \forall a\, :\, V,\; a \in K \implies \neg \left(x = a\right) \implies x \sim_{G} a\), we obtain \((x \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \implies (\forall a_{1}\, :\, V,\; a_{1} \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(K) \implies \neg (x = a_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} a_{1})) = (x \in K \implies (\forall a_{1}\, :\, V,\; a_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = a_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} a_{1}))\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}} with \(\alpha = x \in K\), we obtain \(\neg (\forall x_{1}\, :\, x \in K,\; (x_{2} \mapsto \forall y\, :\, V,\; y \in K \implies \neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y)(x_{1})) \iff (\exists x_{1}\, :\, x \in K,\; \neg (x_{2} \mapsto \forall y\, :\, V,\; y \in K \implies \neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y)(x_{1}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\neg (x \in K \implies (\forall y\, :\, V,\; y \in K \implies \neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y))) = (x \in K \land \neg (\forall y\, :\, V,\; y \in K \implies \neg (x = y) \implies x \sim_{G} y))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x \in K\).
By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}}, we obtain \(\neg (\forall x_{1}\, :\, V,\; (x_{2} \mapsto x_{2} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{2}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{2})(x_{1})) \iff (\exists x_{1}\, :\, V,\; \neg (x_{2} \mapsto x_{2} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{2}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{2})(x_{1}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\neg (\forall x_{1}\, :\, V,\; x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (\exists x_{1}\, :\, V,\; \neg (x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x_{1}\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}} with \(\alpha = x_{1} \in K\), we obtain \(\neg (\forall x_{2}\, :\, x_{1} \in K,\; (x_{3} \mapsto \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})(x_{2})) \iff (\exists x_{2}\, :\, x_{1} \in K,\; \neg (x_{3} \mapsto \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})(x_{2}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\neg (x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (x_{1} \in K \land \neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x_{1} \in K\).
By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6e6f745f666f72616c6c}} with \(\alpha = \neg \left(x = x_{1}\right)\), we obtain \(\neg (\forall x_{2}\, :\, \neg (x = x_{1}),\; (x_{3} \mapsto x \sim_{G} x_{1})(x_{2})) \iff (\exists x_{2}\, :\, \neg (x = x_{1}),\; \neg (x_{3} \mapsto x \sim_{G} x_{1})(x_{2}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
By \paperlink{premise:6578697374735f70726f70}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6578697374735f70726f70}}, we obtain \(\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}) \iff \neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4966662e6f665f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4966662e6f665f6571}}, we obtain \(\neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1}) \iff \neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})\).
\end{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \(\left(x_{1} \in K\right) = \left(x_{1} \in K\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4966662e6f665f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4966662e6f665f6571}}, we obtain \(x_{1} \in K \iff x_{1} \in K\).
By \paperlink{premise:6578697374735f70726f705f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6578697374735f70726f705f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(x_{1} \in K \land \neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1}) \iff x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((x_{1} \in K \land \neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).
By \paperlink{premise:6578697374735f70726f70}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6578697374735f70726f70}}, we obtain \(x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})) \iff x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}))\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1}))) = (x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((x_{1} \in K \land \neg (\neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\neg (x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).
\end{proofstep}
By function extensionality, we obtain \((x_{1} \mapsto \neg (x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (x_{1} \mapsto x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \((\exists x_{1}\, :\, V,\; \neg (x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (\exists x_{1}\, :\, V,\; x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\neg (\forall x_{1}\, :\, V,\; x_{1} \in K \implies \neg (x = x_{1}) \implies x \sim_{G} x_{1})) = (\exists x_{1}\, :\, V,\; x_{1} \in K \land (\neg (x = x_{1}) \land \neg (x \sim_{G} x_{1})))\).

\begin{lemma}[{Exists is turan maximal}]\label{theorem:6}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(r\) be a natural number. Assume \(0 < r\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \exists H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; \operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(H,\allowbreak{} r).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Set \(c\) equal to \(\{H\in \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V) \mid H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\}\).
Choose the witness \(\operatorname{edgeless\,graph}(V)\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(2 \le r + 1\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(\mathrm{true} = \mathrm{true}\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{decide}(\operatorname{is\,Impossible}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(0))) = \mathrm{true}) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:6f665f6465636964655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f665f6465636964655f65715f74727565}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{is\,Impossible}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(0))) = \mathrm{true}\).
Use the hypothesis \(\neg \left(2 \le r + 1\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}}, we obtain \(r + 1 < 2\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(r + 1 < 2\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(r + 1 + 1 \le 2\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}}, we obtain \(0 \le 2 - \left(r + 1 + 1\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(2 = 2\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(2 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}} with \(n = r\) and \(m = 1\), we obtain \(r + 1 = r + 1\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}} in reverse gives \(r = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By definition, we obtain \(1 = 1\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(r + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).

Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(r + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(r + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By definition, we obtain \(1 = 1\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(r + 1 + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}} with \(l_{1} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle)\) and \(l_{2} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)\) and \(v = \operatorname{of\,List}\left(\langle r\rangle\right)\) in reverse gives \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(r + 1 + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(2 - (r + 1 + 1) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) - \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}} with \(l_{1} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)\) and \(l_{2} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle)\) and \(v = \operatorname{of\,List}\left(\langle r\rangle\right)\) in reverse gives \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) - \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(2 - (r + 1 + 1) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:6c655f6f665f6c655f6f665f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6c655f6f665f6c655f6f665f6571}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{Z}\), we obtain \(0 \le \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(-0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle -1\rangle,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{tidy\,Constraint}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle -1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{tidy\,Coeffs}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle -1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle r\rangle)) = \mathrm{true}\).
Use the hypothesis \(0 < r\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(0 < r\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(0 + 1 \le r\).

\section{Is turan maximal}
\begin{lemma}[{Degree equals}]\label{theorem:7}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be elements of \(V\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume \(\neg \left(s \sim_{G} t\right)\). Then \(\deg_{G}(s) = \deg_{G}(t)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
