For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}} with \(p = H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\) and \(q = \left|E(H)\right| \le \left|E(G)\right|\), we obtain \((\neg (H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land \neg (|E(H)| \le |E(G)|))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}} with \(\beta = \mathbb{N}\) and \(a = \left|E(H)\right|\) and \(b = \left|E(G)\right|\), we obtain \((\neg (|E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (|E(G)| < |E(H)|)\).

Assume \(\deg_{G}(s) \ne \deg_{G}(t)\).

By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e656d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e656d}} with \(p = \deg_{G}(t) < \deg_{G}(s)\), we obtain \(\deg_{G}(t) < \deg_{G}(s) \lor \neg \left(\deg_{G}(t) < \deg_{G}(s)\right)\).

By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{tidy\,Constraint}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle -1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 0\rangle)))),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{tidy\,Coeffs}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle -1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 0\rangle)))),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \deg_{G}(t)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \deg_{G}(s)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle |E(\operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s))|\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle |E(G)| + \deg_{G}(t) - \deg_{G}(s)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle |E(G)|\rangle))))) = \mathrm{true}\).

\deg_{G}(s)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle |E(G)|\rangle))))) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{tidy\,Constraint}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(2),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 0\rangle)))),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{tidy\,Coeffs}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Option\mathord{:}some}(2),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 0\rangle)))),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \deg_{G}(t)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \deg_{G}(s)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle |E(\operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s))|\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle |E(G)| + \deg_{G}(t) - \deg_{G}(s)\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle |E(G)|\rangle))))) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}}, we obtain \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
The two alternatives exhaust the cases. Hence \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
The contrary assumption leads to a contradiction. Hence \(\left|E(G)\right| < \left|E(\operatorname{clone}(G, t, s))\right|\).
Combining the two conclusions, we obtain \(\operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s)\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land |E(G)| < |E(\operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s))|\).
This witness proves existence. Hence \(\exists \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}(\operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s))),\; \operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s)\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land |E(G)| < |E(\operatorname{clone}(G,\allowbreak{} t,\allowbreak{} s))|\).
This witness proves existence. Hence \(\exists H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \exists \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land |E(G)| < |E(H)|\).
\end{proofstep}
The two alternatives exhaust the cases. Hence \(\exists H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \exists \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land |E(G)| < |E(H)|\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}}, \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f616e645f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f616e645f6571}}, \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}}, \paperlink{premise:66756e657874}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:66756e657874}} and the identity established above in the preceding result gives \(\neg (\deg_{G}(s) = \deg_{G}(t)) \implies \neg (G\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land (\forall H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \forall \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{defeq:1}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:1}} in the preceding result gives \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land (\forall H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \forall \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}}, we obtain \(\deg_{G}(s) = \deg_{G}(t)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[{Not adj trans}]\label{theorem:8}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(s\), \(t\), and \(u\) be elements of \(V\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume \(\neg \left(t \sim_{G} s\right)\). Assume \(\neg \left(s \sim_{G} u\right)\). Then \(\neg \left(t \sim_{G} u\right)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Assume \(s \sim_{G} t\).
Use the hypothesis \(s \sim_{G} t\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e41646a2e73796d6d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e41646a2e73796d6d}}, we obtain \(t \sim_{G} s\).
Applying the hypothesis \(\neg \left(t \sim_{G} s\right)\), we obtain \(\mathrm{False}\).
By \paperlink{theorem:7}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:7}}, we obtain \(\deg_{G}(s) = \deg_{G}(t)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:7}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:7}}, we obtain \(\deg_{G}(s) = \deg_{G}(u)\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(H\) in \(\operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f666f72616c6c5f6571}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}\left(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}\right)\) and \(\mathit{inst}_{2} \mapsto H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|\) in place of its parameter \(s\), we obtain \((\neg (\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (\exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; \neg (H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f696d706c6965735f6571}} with \(p = H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\) and \(q = \left|E(H)\right| \le \left|E(G)\right|\), we obtain \((\neg (H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land \neg (|E(H)| \le |E(G)|))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}} with \(\beta = \mathbb{N}\) and \(a = \left|E(H)\right|\) and \(b = \left|E(G)\right|\), we obtain \((\neg (|E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (|E(G)| < |E(H)|)\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \((H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land \neg (|E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land |E(G)| < |E(H)|)\).

\begin{theorem}[{Equivalence not adj}]\label{theorem:9}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Equivalence}(\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2})).\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Reflexivity.}\enspace
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e69727265666c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e69727265666c}}, we obtain \(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} x\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}}, we obtain \(\left(x \sim_{G} x\right) = \mathrm{False}\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \(\left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} x\right)\right) = \left(\neg \mathrm{False}\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, we obtain \(\left(\neg \mathrm{False}\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(\left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} x\right)\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
\end{proofstep}
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}}, \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f74727565}} and the identity established above gives \(\forall x\, :\, V,\; (\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))(x,\allowbreak{} x)\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Symmetry.}\enspace
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(V\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(y\) in \(V\).
By definition, we obtain \(\left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\right) = \left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e61646a5f636f6d6d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e61646a5f636f6d6d}} with \(u = y\) and \(v = x\), we obtain \(y \sim_{G} x \iff x \sim_{G} y\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(\left(y \sim_{G} x\right) = \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \(\left(\neg \left(y \sim_{G} x\right)\right) = \left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}} with \(p_{1} = \neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\) and \(p_{2} = \neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\) and \(q_{1} = \neg \left(y \sim_{G} x\right)\) and \(q_{2} = \neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\), we obtain \((\neg (x \sim_{G} y) \implies \neg (y \sim_{G} x)) = (\neg (x \sim_{G} y) \implies \neg (x \sim_{G} y))\).
By \paperlink{premise:696d705f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d705f73656c66}}, we obtain \(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right) \implies \neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right) \iff \mathrm{True}\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \(\left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right) \implies \neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right)\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(\left(\neg \left(x \sim_{G} y\right) \implies \neg \left(y \sim_{G} x\right)\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \((\forall a\, :\, V,\; \neg (x \sim_{G} a) \implies \neg (a \sim_{G} x)) = (\forall a\, :\, V,\; \mathrm{True})\).
By \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f74727565}} with \(\alpha = V\), we obtain \(\left(\forall a\, :\, V,\; \mathrm{True}\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\forall a\, :\, V,\; \neg (x \sim_{G} a) \implies \neg (a \sim_{G} x)) = \mathrm{True}\).
\end{proofstep}
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}}, \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f74727565}} and the identity established above gives \(\forall x\, :\, V,\; \forall y\, :\, V,\; (\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))(x,\allowbreak{} y) \implies (\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))(y,\allowbreak{} x)\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Transitivity.}\enspace
Fix \(x\) in \(V\).
Fix \(y\) in \(V\).
Fix \(z\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{theorem:8}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:8}}, we obtain \((\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))(x,\allowbreak{} y) \implies (\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))(y,\allowbreak{} z) \implies (\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))(x,\allowbreak{} z)\).
These properties establish \(\operatorname{Equivalence}(\mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \neg (\mathit{x1} \sim_{G} \mathit{x2}))\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[{Not adj if and only if part equals}]\label{theorem:10}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(s\) and \(t\) be elements of \(V\). Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume equality on \(V\) is decidable. Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \neg (s \sim_{G} t) \iff \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} t).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Set \(\mathit{fp}\) equal to \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:65715f636f6d6d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f636f6d6d}}, \paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6966665f706172745f65715f70617274}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6966665f706172745f65715f70617274}} and \paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e6d656d5f756e6976}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e7365742e6d656d5f756e6976}} gives \(t \in \operatorname{part}(\mathit{fp},\allowbreak{} s) \iff \operatorname{part}(\mathit{fp},\allowbreak{} s) = \operatorname{part}(\mathit{fp},\allowbreak{} t)\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(t \in \operatorname{part}(\text{the partition into equivalence classes of }\operatorname{nonadjacency\,relation}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s) \iff \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} t)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6f665365746f69645f6966665f72656c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6d656d5f706172745f6f665365746f69645f6966665f72656c}} in the preceding result gives \(s \sim_{\operatorname{nonadjacency\,relation}(G,\allowbreak{} r)} t \iff \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} t)\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\neg (s \sim_{G} t) \iff \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} t)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[{Degree equals cardinality difference part cardinality}]\label{theorem:11}

By \paperlink{premise:65715f747375625f6f665f6164645f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f747375625f6f665f6164645f6571}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\), we obtain \(|\{t\in V \mid s \sim_{G} t\}| = |V| - |\{t\in V \mid \neg (s \sim_{G} t)\}|\).

Substituting equals, we obtain \(|V| - |\{t\in V \mid \neg (s \sim_{G} t)\}| = |V| - |\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s)|\).
\par Combining these equalities gives \(\deg_{G}(s) = |V| - |\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} s)|\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[{Is equipartition}]\label{theorem:12}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume equality on \(V\) is decidable. Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Equipartition}\left(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\right)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}

The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r) = \mathit{fp}\).

\begin{proofstep}

Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\neg (\forall x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|)) = (\exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land |E(G)| < |E(H)|)\).

\begin{lemma}[{Cardinality parts at most}]\label{theorem:13}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume equality on \(V\) is decidable. Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| \le r.\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg (|\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| \le r)\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7375627365745f706172745f62696a4f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7375627365745f706172745f62696a4f6e}} with \(s = V\) and \(P = \operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\), we obtain \(\exists r_{1}\, :\, \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V),\; r_{1} \subseteq V \land \operatorname{Bij\,On}(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(r_{1}),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))))\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(z\) in \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V)\).
Assume \(z \subseteq V \land \operatorname{Bij\,On}(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))))\).
Use the hypothesis \(z \subseteq V \land \operatorname{Bij\,On}(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))))\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(z \subseteq V\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Bij\,On}(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))))\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Clique property.}\enspace
Fix \(v\) in \(V\).
Assume \(v \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z)\).
Fix \(w\) in \(V\).
Assume \(w \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z)\).
Assume \(v \ne w\).
Assume \(\neg \left(v \sim_{G} w\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Bij\,On}(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{underlying\,set}(\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))))\).
Use the hypothesis \(v \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z)\).
Use the hypothesis \(w \in \operatorname{underlying\,set}(z)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\neg \left(v \sim_{G} w\right)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{theorem:10}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:10}} (using \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\)) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} v) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} w)\).
By \paperlink{premise:5365742e42696a4f6e2e696e6a4f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:5365742e42696a4f6e2e696e6a4f6e}} with \(\beta = \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V)\), we obtain \(v = w\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696d706c6965735f636f6e6772}} and \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}} in the preceding result gives \(\neg \left(v \sim_{G} w\right) \implies \neg \left(v \ne w\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(v \ne w\).
By \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e436f6e747261706f73652e6d7472}}, we obtain \(v \sim_{G} w\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Cardinality.}\enspace
By definition, we obtain \(\left|z\right| = \left|z\right|\).
These properties establish \(z\text{ is a clique of size }\left|z\right|\text{ in }G\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e49734e436c697175652e6e6f745f636c6971756546726565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e49734e436c697175652e6e6f745f636c6971756546726565}}, we obtain \(G\text{ contains a clique of size }\left|z\right|\).
Use the hypothesis \(\neg (|\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| \le r)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c655f6571}} in the preceding result gives \(r < \left|\operatorname{parts}\left(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\right)\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:4e61742e737563635f6c655f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e737563635f6c655f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(r + 1 \le \left|\operatorname{parts}\left(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\right)\right|\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
Taking the first conjunct, we obtain \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e436c69717565467265652e6d6f6e6f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e436c69717565467265652e6d6f6e6f}}, we obtain \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }|\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\).
Use the previously proved fact \(G\text{ contains a clique of size }\left|z\right|\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f65715f6f665f6571756976}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e7365742e636172645f65715f6f665f6571756976}} in the preceding result gives \(G\text{ contains a clique of size }|\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\).
The assertion contradicts its negation. Hence \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
Using the two conjuncts, we obtain \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
Using the existential hypothesis, we obtain \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
The contrary assumption leads to a contradiction. Hence \(\left|\operatorname{parts}\left(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\right)\right| \le r\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[{Cardinality parts}]\label{theorem:14}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Assume equality on \(V\) is decidable. Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Set \(\mathit{fp}\) equal to \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r) = \mathit{fp}\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r) = \mathit{fp}\).
\end{proofstep}
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Upper bound.}\enspace

\begin{lemma}[{Turán's theorem (forward direction)}]\label{theorem:15}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Then \(G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:12}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:12}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Is\,Equipartition}\left(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G, r)\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e497345717569706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7061727450726573657276696e674571756976}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e706172746974696f6e2e497345717569706172746974696f6e2e6578697374735f7061727450726573657276696e674571756976}} with \(s = V\), we obtain \(\exists f\, :\, \operatorname{Bij}(\{\langle v,\; v\in V\rangle\mid v\in V\},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Fin}(|\{v\mid v\in V\}|)),\; \forall a\, :\, V,\; \forall b\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{val}(f(a)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{val}(f(b)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(\mathit{zm}\) in \(\operatorname{Bij}(\{\langle v,\; v\in V\rangle\mid v\in V\},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Fin}(|\{v\mid v\in V\}|))\).
Assume \(\forall a\, :\, V,\; \forall b\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(a)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(b)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\).
Choose the witness \(\text{the graph isomorphism with vertex map }(x\mapsto \mathit{zm}(\langle x,\; x\in V\rangle))\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Preservation and reflection of the relation.}\enspace
Fix \(a\) in \(V\).
Fix \(b\) in \(V\).
Applying the hypothesis \(\forall a\, :\, V,\; \forall b\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(a)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(b)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\), we obtain \(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\).
By \paperlink{premise:6c655f6f725f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6c655f6f725f6c74}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\) and \(r\) in place of its parameter \(a\) and \(\left|V\right|\) in place of its parameter \(b\), we obtain \(r \le \left|V\right| \lor \left|V\right| < r\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(r \le \left|V\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:4966662e72666c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4966662e72666c}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6d696e5f65715f7269676874}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6d696e5f65715f7269676874}} (using \(r \le \left|V\right|\)) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r) = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r)\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\left|V\right| < r\).
Fix \(x\) in \(V\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e2e69734c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e2e69734c74}} with \(\mathit{self} = \mathit{zm}\left(\left\langle x,\; x\in V\right\rangle\right)\), we obtain \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}\left(\left\langle x,\; x\in V\right\rangle\right)) < \left|V\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:4966662e72666c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4966662e72666c}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}}, \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}} (using \(\left|V\right| < r\)) and \(\forall x\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle x,\; x\in V\rangle)) < |V|\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}}, \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e7472616e73}} (using \(\left|V\right| < r\)) and \(\forall x\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle x,\; x\in V\rangle)) < |V|\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}} and \(\forall x\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle x,\; x\in V\rangle)) < |V|\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod |V|\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6d6f645f65715f6f665f6c74}} and \(\forall x\, :\, V,\; \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle x,\; x\in V\rangle)) < |V|\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod |V| = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod |V|\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6d696e5f65715f6c656674}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6d696e5f65715f6c656674}} and \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}} (using \(\left|V\right| < r\)) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r) = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r)\).
\end{proofstep}
The two alternatives exhaust the cases. Hence \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r) = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod \operatorname{min}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{theorem:14}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:14}} (using \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\)) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\).
Rewriting with propositional extensionality, \paperlink{theorem:10}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:10}}, \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\), \(\operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} a) = \operatorname{part}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r),\allowbreak{} b) \iff \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))| = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod |\operatorname{parts}(\operatorname{nonadjacency\,partition}(G,\allowbreak{} r))|\) and substitution of equals in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r = \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff \neg (a \sim_{G} b)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f6e655f696666}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f6e655f696666}} in the preceding result gives \(\neg (\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r) \iff \neg (a \sim_{G} b)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f6966665f6e6f74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f6966665f6e6f74}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff a \sim_{G} b\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff a \sim_{G} b\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \ne \operatorname{val}(\mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle)) \bmod r \iff a \sim_{G} b\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\mathit{zm}(\langle a,\; a\in V\rangle) \sim_{\operatorname{turan\,Graph}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r)} \mathit{zm}(\langle b,\; b\in V\rangle) \iff a \sim_{G} b\).
This element witnesses nonemptiness. Hence \(G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Using the existential hypothesis, we obtain \(G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
\end{proof}

\section{Simple graphs}
\begin{lemma}[{Turán's theorem (reverse direction)}]\label{theorem:16}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(n\) and \(r\) be natural numbers. Let \(f\) be a graph isomorphism from \(G\) to \(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(n, r\right)\). Assume \(0 < r\). Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:6}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:6}}, we obtain \(\exists H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; \operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(H,\allowbreak{} r)\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(J\) in \(\operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V)\).
Assume \(\exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{J}),\; \operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(J,\allowbreak{} r)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\exists x\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{J}),\; \operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(J,\allowbreak{} r)\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(w\) in \(\operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}\left(\operatorname{Adj}_{J}\right)\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(J, r\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:15}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:15}}, we obtain \(J \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
Consider the possible forms of \(J \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
\emph{Intro case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(g\) in \(\operatorname{Iso}\left(J, \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:4}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:4}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(n, r\right)\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e436c69717565467265652e636f6d6170}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e436c69717565467265652e636f6d6170}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\) and \(\operatorname{to\,Rel\,Embedding}\left(f\right)\) in place of its parameter \(f\), we obtain \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(H\) in \(\operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V)\).
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}\left(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}\right)\).
Assume \(H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(J, r\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1\).
Taking the second conjunct, we obtain \(\left|E(H)\right| \le \left|E(J)\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e49736f2e636172645f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e49736f2e636172645f6571}} with \(W = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\) and the given \(f\), we obtain \(\left|V\right| = \left|\operatorname{Fin}(n)\right|\).
By \paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f66696e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f66696e}} with the given \(n\), we obtain \(\left|\operatorname{Fin}(n)\right| = n\).
After substitution, \(g\) has type \(\operatorname{Iso}\left(J, \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(n, r\right)\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e49736f2e636172645f6564676546696e7365745f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:53696d706c6547726170682e49736f2e636172645f6564676546696e7365745f6571}} with \(f^{-1} \circ (g\, :\, \operatorname{Iso}(J,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{turan\,Graph}(n,\allowbreak{} r)))\) in place of its parameter \(f\), we obtain \(\left|E(J)\right| = \left|E(G)\right|\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\left|E(H)\right| \le \left|E(G)\right|\).
\end{proofstep}
Combining the two conclusions, we obtain \(G\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \land (\forall H\, :\, \operatorname{Simple\,Graph}(V),\; \forall \mathit{inst}_{2}\, :\, \operatorname{Decidable\,Rel}(\operatorname{Adj}_{H}),\; H\text{ contains no clique of size }r + 1 \implies |E(H)| \le |E(G)|)\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Using the existential hypothesis, we obtain \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Using the existential hypothesis, we obtain \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[{Iso}]\label{theorem:17}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Let \(W\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(W\). Let \(H\) be a simple graph on \(W\). Assume adjacency in \(H\) is decidable. Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\). Let \(f\) be a graph isomorphism from \(G\) to \(H\). Assume \(0 < r\). Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(H, r\right)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \paperlink{theorem:16}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:16}} with \(\operatorname{Nonempty\mathord{:}some} \circ f^{-1}\) in place of its parameter \(f\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[{Is turan maximal turan graph}]\label{theorem:18}
Let \(n\) and \(r\) be natural numbers. Assume \(0 < r\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(\operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(n, r\right), r\right).\)
\end{center}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \paperlink{theorem:16}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:16}} with \(V = \operatorname{Fin}(n)\) and \(f = \operatorname{Simple\,Graph\mathord{:}Iso\mathord{:}refl}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[{Turán's theorem}]\label{theorem:19}
Let \(V\) be a type. Fix a finite enumeration of \(V\). Let \(G\) be a simple graph on \(V\). Assume adjacency in \(G\) is decidable. Let \(r\) be a natural number. Assume \(0 < r\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(G,\allowbreak{} r) \iff G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r).\)
\end{center}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:15}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:15}}, we obtain \(G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}\left(\left|V\right|, r\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:16}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:16}} with \(f = \operatorname{Nonempty\mathord{:}some}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}\left(G, r\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Together the two implications give the equivalence. Hence \(\operatorname{Is\,Turan\,Maximal}(G,\allowbreak{} r) \iff G \cong \operatorname{turan\,Graph}(|V|,\allowbreak{} r)\).
\end{proof}
